title: KV residency zoning with serpentine slot packing and adaptive slit defrag
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: Under continuous batching workloads we observe persistent micro-fragmentation in the GPU-resident KV cache. Short-lived token entries created by chat-like workloads cause allocation holes and uneven slot utilization, which increases eviction churn during peak batching windows and elevates tail latency for cold keys. Existing slab and pool approaches reduce worst-case fragmentation but either over-reserve memory or force heavy background compaction that interferes with inference throughput.

Proposal summary: Introduce a KV "residency zoning" allocator that groups entries by recent residency (hot/warm/cold) and uses a serpentine slot-packing layout inside zones to reduce cross-zone fragmentation. Complement this with an "adaptive slit defrag" background worker: low-cost micro-moves that stitch adjacent holes during low GPU utilization and align relocations to batch boundaries to avoid KV race with active in-flight requests. The design prioritizes incremental, throughput-friendly healing over large rewrites.

Key ideas: 
- Residency zones: small fixed-size regions for hot, warm, cold residency classes, with hot region prioritized for placement and pinning. Zones have dynamic soft quotas that adapt to observed residency curves.
- Serpentine slot packing: within a zone, allocate with a zig-zag placement pattern (serpentine) to bias adjacent free slots to be co-located for lightweight stitching and to avoid long linear holes that block large inserts.
- Adaptive slit defrag: a background worker that performs micro-relocations (single-slot or short-range copies) when the system detects a sequence of small holes. Movements are scheduled to execute only when batch windows are idle or when GPU utilization < threshold.
- Batch-aware relocation epochs: coalesce relocations into epochs aligned with batch boundaries and KV flush points so that KV cache KV hot-swapping doesn't contend with inference token streams.
- Admission & backpressure: when fragmentation ratio exceeds target and healing is insufficient, temporarily apply per-request admission controls (slower batching or preferring alternative model variants) to protect latency SLOs.

Telemetry & metrics to add: fragmentation_ratio (holes_bytes / total_alloc_bytes), zone_utilization_{hot,warm,cold}, serpentine-coalescence-events, slit_defrag_ops, avg_relocation_size_bytes, defrag_cpu_ms, defrag_gpu_ms, tail_latency_95/99 during defrag, and live eviction churn per minute.

Why unique: Unlike full slab compaction or global buddy moves, this approach is residency-aware and performs amortized micro-moves aligned to runtime batch semantics to minimize throughput regressions. The serpentine packing reduces formation of long contiguous holes, making micro-defrag effective.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation_ratio reduced by >= 35% on chat-like workload (sustained 1k rps continuous batching) compared to baseline
Tail latency (P99) during steady-state and defrag windows does not regress by more than 5% vs baseline SLO
Defrag CPU/GPU overhead remains < 3% of baseline compute for sustained experiment window (1 hour)
Telemetry exposed in Console: zone_utilization metrics, fragment heatmap, and a defrag activity timeline
Feature gated with rollout flag and ability to disable background defrag and serpentine packing independently
implementation_steps: Design phase (1 week): finalize in-memory layout for serpentine packing and define zone soft quotas; review with runtime and perf teams
Prototype allocator hooks (2 weeks): implement zone creation and serpentine placement in a feature branch; add unit tests for allocation patterns
Background worker (1 week): implement adaptive slit defrag worker with scheduling tied to batch idle events and util thresholds
Telemetry & dashboards (3 days): add fragmentation and relocation metrics; wire into Console experiment dashboard
Benchmarking (1 week): run sustained chat-like continuous batching tests across representative model sizes (1B, 7B, 70B) and GPU types; collect overhead and fragmentation numbers
Canary rollout (2 weeks): enable for 10% of traffic on dedicated cluster, monitor KPIs and abort criteria
Full rollout & cleanup (1 week): ship runtime flag default-on for targeted customers, add docs and runbook for troubleshooting
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Micro-relocations could compete with inference for GPU memory bandwidth -> Mitigation: schedule relocations only when batch windows are idle and cap relocation throughput per-second
Risk: Serpentine packing complexity may introduce allocation bugs -> Mitigation: extensive unit tests, small canary, memory sanitizer coverage
Risk: Hot/warm misclassification could misplace long-lived tokens -> Mitigation: use conservative hysteresis for zone transitions and monitor zone churn metrics
Risk: Unexpected latency spikes during defrag -> Mitigation: automatic rollback thresholds and conservative default limits; provide toggle to disable defrag on a per-cluster basis

notes: This ticket focuses on production-friendly, low-latency healing rather than aggressive compaction. If results are insufficient, follow-up work will evaluate lightweight relocation combined with epochal snapshot rewrites.
